statement: For every relative-error rounding model and every finite ordered binary tree whose leaves are pairs of real numbers, if (h+1)u<1, where h is the tree depth and u is the model error bound, the computed reduction of rounded leaf products equals the exact sum of a tree of perturbed exact leaf products with the same shape. Each leaf product x is replaced by a real y satisfying |y-x| <= ((h+1)u/(1-(h+1)u))|x|. The perturbations are of the product values; the statement does not construct perturbations of the two factors separately.

targets.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.roundedDotProduct_exists_perturbation
targets.statement: For every model M : Research.FloatingPoint.Model and every t : Tree(R × R), let u=M.u and h=depth(t) in N, with depth(leaf(a,b))=0 and depth(node(L,R))=1+max(depth(L),depth(R)). A model contains a real u>=0 and a function r:R->R such that for every z in R there exists a real delta with |delta|<=u and r(z)=z(1+delta). If (h+1)u<1 (the natural number h+1 is viewed as a real in this inequality), then there exists a tree P : Tree(R) such that IsPerturbation(gamma(h+1,u), exactProductTree(t), P) and exactSum(P)=roundedDotProduct(M,t). Here gamma(k,u)=ku/(1-ku) for k in N, using the real value of k. The perturbation relation requires identical ordered tree shape and, for every pair of corresponding leaf values x of exactProductTree(t) and y of P, |y-x|<=gamma(h+1,u)|x|; its node clause applies this same bound recursively to both children. Thus if the leaves of t, in order, are (a_i,b_i), i=1,...,n, there are y_i in R on the same tree shape with |y_i-a_i b_i|<=((h+1)u/(1-(h+1)u))|a_i b_i| for every i and sum_{i=1}^n y_i=roundedDotProduct(M,t). The sum is exact real addition. Tree(R × R) consists of finite nonempty trees generated by leaves and binary nodes, so n>=1; no balance or equal leaf-depth hypothesis is imposed. The right-hand side is obtained by applying r to each exact product a_i b_i and then recursively applying r to each sum of the two child results according to t. The bound uses the original tree depth plus one; mapping products preserves that depth. The existential tree P need not equal roundedProductTree(M,t), since its leaf values also account for errors from internal additions.

constructions.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.exactProductTree
constructions.description: A function Tree(R × R)->Tree(R). It maps each leaf labelled by (a,b) to a leaf labelled by the exact real product ab and preserves every binary node: E(leaf(a,b))=leaf(ab), E(node(L,R))=node(E(L),E(R)). It does not multiply values across different leaves or combine the internal nodes. In the target theorem this is the reference tree whose leaf values are perturbed.

constructions.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.roundedProductTree
constructions.description: For every model M with rounding function r, a function Tree(R × R)->Tree(R) that preserves the entire tree shape and replaces each leaf (a,b) by M.mul(a,b)=r(ab): Q_M(leaf(a,b))=leaf(r(ab)), Q_M(node(L,R))=node(Q_M(L),Q_M(R)). Each leaf multiplication uses exact real multiplication followed by one application of r. There is no separate rounding of a or b and no addition in this construction. This is the intermediate tree passed to roundedSum by roundedDotProduct.

constructions.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.roundedDotProduct
constructions.description: A function taking M : Research.FloatingPoint.Model and t : Tree(R × R) to a real number. It is defined as roundedSum(M,roundedProductTree(M,t)). With r=M.round its full recursion is D_M(leaf(a,b))=r(ab) and D_M(node(L,R))=r(D_M(L)+D_M(R)). The auxiliary roundedSum returns a real leaf value unchanged and applies M.add(x,y)=r(x+y) at each internal node. Thus this construction rounds every leaf product once and every internal addition once in the given tree order; it does not choose or balance a reduction tree. A leaf at depth d from the root contributes along a path with one multiplication rounding and d addition roundings; h is the maximum such d. The target theorem represents this returned real exactly as exactSum of an existential perturbation of exactProductTree(t), with the common leaf bound gamma(h+1,M.u).

assumptions: The model parameter is arbitrary subject to its defining data: u is a real number with 0<=u; r is a function R->R; for every real z there exists a real delta, potentially depending on z, such that |delta|<=u and r(z)=z(1+delta). No further representable-number set, radix, precision, rounding rule, or independence condition is specified.

The input t is any finite nonempty ordered binary tree with a pair of arbitrary real numbers at each leaf. Nodes each have exactly two children. There are no sign, nonzero, magnitude, balance, or fixed-size restrictions on the leaves or tree.
The target requires (depth(t)+1)u<1, with the natural depth cast to a real for multiplication. Together with u>=0 this makes the stated gamma denominator positive and its bound nonnegative.

The auxiliary definitions are depth(leaf(x))=0 and depth(node(L,R))=1+max(depth(L),depth(R)); exactSum(leaf(x))=x and exactSum(node(L,R))=exactSum(L)+exactSum(R), using exact real addition; and gamma(k,u)=ku/(1-ku) for natural k and real u.

For any real bound b, IsPerturbation(b,X,Y) is inductively generated by the leaf rule |y-x|<=b|x| for X=leaf(x), Y=leaf(y), and the node rule requiring IsPerturbation(b,L,L') and IsPerturbation(b,R,R') for X=node(L,R), Y=node(L',R'). It preserves shape and child order. In particular an exact product of zero must have perturbed value zero.
